result.title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
result.summary: Long-term memory enables language-model agents to personalize future interactions, but a finite memory bank cannot preserve every extracted fact. Existing memory gating policies are typically shared across users and therefore fail to account for user-specific patterns of future reuse. In this paper, we study memory gating at the fact level. We first propose a retrieval-based labeling strategy that labels each fact by whether it is later retrieved and incorporated into responses. We then formulate online memory gating as contextual apple tasting with delayed one-sided feedback, and propose Warm-Start UCB, which combines offline learning from existing data with online adaptation to the current user. Our theoretical analysis establishes a high-probability regret upper bound of $\tilde{O}(Tε\wedge d\sqrt{T})$ when the delay window is at most $O(\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ is the total number of rounds, $ε$ is the initialization error, $d$ is the dimension of the feature map, and $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides constant and poly-logarithmic factors. The results of our experiment demonstrate that our method outperforms all baselines under different memory budgets and history lengths, establishing it as a promising personalized memory gating policy.

AI.brief_summary: 本文研究事实级别的个性化记忆门控：先用「后续是否被检索并写入回答」来标注每个事实，再把在线门控建模为延迟单边反馈下的 contextual apple tasting，提出结合离线预热与在线自适应的 Warm-Start UCB，并给出遗憾上界与实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有限记忆库该保留哪些事实、何时会被重用」的决策，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、是否保留特定 latent 内容以及 STOP 决策的价值判断存在概念联系；延迟单边反馈下的信用分配也可供核查，但领域较远，迁移性待验证。
